records.summary: Router work needs route-config, route-tree, route-context, viewport, viewport-agent, routeable-component, and route-recognizer semantics before product features rely on it.
records.rationale: External apps are pressure floors, not literal specs. Router modeling must be grounded in the Aurelia framework router architecture because semantic-runtime will eventually support MCP, IDE, AOT, SSR, and SSG.
guidance: Start with framework.router flow and relationship projections before deriving product router behavior from an app sample.

Router URL parsing and stringifying are first-class `framework.router` flow rows under the `url-parsing` stage with `url-parser` relationship mechanisms; do not treat route-recognizer rows as the whole navigation URL story.

Treat `framework.router:flow-issues` and `framework.router:recognizer-issues` as map freshness checks too: source-baseline and descriptor-count drift are issue rows, not only materialization warnings.
Use `pnpm --filter @aurelia-ls/atlas framework:router -- --projection=relationships --query=ViewportAgent --detail` when row-level router grounding is needed beyond the compact pressure summary.

Use `pnpm --filter @aurelia-ls/atlas bridge:aulink -- --projection=mirror --packageId=router --detail` when the question is whether router framework actors have product mirrors, role evidence, or emulation obligations.
Model au-viewport explicitly when route rendering semantics are in scope.
Treat route-recognizer as a potentially wide substrate task, similar in complexity to expression or attribute parsing.

Runtime-state-specific recursive expansion is a prerequisite for router/viewport work only when the product asks for per-activation truth such as exact active viewport trees, activation/reuse/deactivate ordering, SSR/SSG route render output, or route-driven stateful recursive component expansion. Static route config, recognizer, route tree, parameter, typed navigation, and authoring guidance should remain finite and definition-level when possible.

Router raw Error rows in ComponentAgent, ViewportInstructionTree.toUrl, and ViewportAgent._canUnload are intentionally unclaimed live state-machine guards as of 2026-05-14; do not turn them into diagnostics unless semantic-runtime grows the corresponding imperative navigation/controller-state emulator.

records.summary: RouteConfigKernelEmitter publishes source contributions and validation evidence; RouteConfigConvergenceProjectPass owns effective definition and applied-use products.
records.rationale: Authored route arrays, decorators, static defaults, configure calls, and hooks need exact source products before effective framework semantics can be computed. Recognition and convergence are now deliberately separate: the emitter preserves source form and issues, while one downstream pass spends resource identity and execution evidence through _create and _applyChildRouteConfig semantics.
guidance: Start in RouteConfigKernelEmitter for authored contribution, routeable component/fallback, child-route, validation, source-address, or field-provenance problems. Start in RouteConfigConvergenceProjectPass for winner selection, framework defaults, repeated-use identity, parent inheritance, openness, or effective consumer behavior.
Do not restore the old hybrid RouteConfig product or let route-context, recognizer, topology, completion, or API consumers reconstruct _create/_applyChildRouteConfig precedence.

Spend router validation codes only for statically closed values matching validation.ts: rtInvalidConfigProperty / AUR3554 for invalid property values and rtInvalidConfig / AUR3555 for null config objects. Weak or external values stay open.

Route object vocabulary is validation authority too: unknown ordinary route-config keys spend rtUnknownConfigProperty / AUR3556, while redirect route objects only allow path and redirectTo and spend rtUnknownRedirectConfigProperty / AUR3557 for everything else.

Spend RouteConfigContext._configureChildRoutes authority for source-backed child route objects whose component is a lazy import and whose path property is absent: rcNoPathLazyImport / AUR3173 belongs in recognition, not route-tree materialization.

Spend RouteContext._resolveLazy invalid-import authority only for definitely invalid lazy-import fulfillments. If imported source is present but the resource is invisible, inspect shared project-evaluation publication and resource admission before adding router-local scanning.
String routeable resolution consumes ResourceDefinitionIndex names, aliases, and dependency-scoped lookup. Keep unresolved strings referential/open instead of inventing component identities.

Origin kind and value kind belong to contributions. Stage, closure, normalized fields, and open fields belong to effective products and reach the public Routes row only through the contribution/effective join.

RouteContextParameterReadMaterializer resolves an enclosing class through its module-local custom-element definition and joins effective route configs by resource target identity. Class names are presentation facts only; same-named routeables in different modules must remain isolated.

A getRouteParameters call inherited from a shared base class can have multiple routed owners. RouteContextParameterReadMaterializer inverts the existing TypeSystem prototype chain over routed resource identities, publishes one read row per known owner with direct/inherited/unmatched ownership and known-owner cardinality, and never unions descendant parameter domains. Multiple proven routed owners publish one semantic-authoring-policy RouterIssue at the base call with concrete route sources as related information; a single inherited owner remains warning-free.
Keep route-config convergence separate from route-tree transition, route-context topology, and route-recognizer state graph semantics.
Use framework.router route-config, routeable-component, route-context, and viewport-agent projections before changing product router behavior.

records.summary: RouteRecognizerStateGraphBuilder is the current product pressure point for route-recognizer graph semantics.
records.rationale: Route-recognizer has a high complexity ceiling similar to parsers. Product behavior should be grounded in framework.router recognizer rows before app samples drive assumptions.
guidance: Start from framework.router recognizer and recognizer-issues projections.

Check `framework.errors` with `gap=raw-error-usage` and `projection=semantic-raw-references` when route-recognizer semantics become diagnostic or policy work; route-recognizer currently exposes message-expression raw Error usage rather than framework ErrorNames.

Known framework-throwing recognizer registration conditions should become RouteRecognizerIssue products and API rows, not open seams or silently accepted graphs. Since @aurelia/route-recognizer throws raw Error instances rather than mapped AUR codes, expose modeled issues as framework-runtime-behavior, keep framework-error-code null, and cite exact `frameworkRawErrorAuthority(...)` constants when the framework throw site is part of `framework.errors`.

Reserved `$$residue` parameter usage and invalid route-parameter regex constraints are registration issues; do not materialize endpoint/state graph products for paths the framework would reject during `RouteRecognizer.$add(...)`.

Route pattern, endpoint, and recognized-route API rows now preserve parameter-name groups. Recognized-route and route-node rows preserve decoded parameter values, recursive residual child recognition publishes nested child recognized routes from routed child RouteConfigContexts, and route-node rows expose child-first / parent-first / append / by-route aggregates over the materialized route-node parent chain. Closed static query params flow through ViewportInstructionTree, RouteTree, and RouteNode rows; repeated query keys stay visible as row entries and as multi-value aggregate arrays in include-query strategies. Include-query append/by-route rows intentionally repeat shared query values per active route node because Aurelia writes ViewportInstructionTree query params onto every node before route-context aggregation. Route-config, router-viewport, viewport-instruction-tree, route-node, component-agent, and router-options rows carry enough named viewport/query/fragment/activeClass shape for generated recipes to verify sibling viewport-instruction targets, low-boilerplate active link styling, and static include-query route parameter reads. Start from those rows when an app-pattern fixture needs static parameter or viewport contract verification. The `router-active-link-state` pressure fixture proves `load.active.bind` as a controller-view-model from-view raw-property channel and `active.class` as a normal class-toggle channel; dynamic query merging, broader live active-navigation state, and viewport activation remain route-context/runtime frontiers.
Treat endpoint registration, path grammar, state graph, candidate selection, and cache behavior as separate semantic axes.
Do not collapse recognizer work into generic route-config traversal.

records.summary: RouteTreeTransitionMaterializationFrame owns planned pre-activation route trees, redirect diagnostics, and sole-candidate route-node handoff.
records.rationale: Route tree work overlaps controller semantics, viewport-agent candidates, routeable components, recursive rendering, and framework-thrown router errors. Planned products are stronger than potential topology but do not prove live availability, guards, scheduling, activation, or successful navigation.
guidance: Check framework.router route-tree, ViewportAgent, and relationship rows before changing planned route-tree materialization.
RouteableComponent is a converged framework concept: preserve authored spelling and resolved custom-element name, and spend the resolved name for viewport compatibility.
Keep au-viewport semantics explicit when route rendering or recursive hydration is involved.

RouteTree redirect-parameter migration accepts only Segment / slash-scoped Segment RouteExpression chains. Sibling composites and grouped expressions belong in RouterIssue rows with exact router exprUnexpectedKind / AUR3502 authority, not route-recognizer rows or generic open seams.

Closed static redirect targets must carry redirectSourceRouteConfig from RouteRecognizer expansion into RouteTree compilation. Use that exact edge to suppress generic redirect-target open seams only when the redirect target was actually re-recognized.
Unknown static redirect targets belong to instrUnknownRedirect / AUR3402 RouterIssue rows from redirect expansion, not to generic redirect-target open seams.

Residual parent-route matches should follow the residual child ViewportInstruction through the resolved child RouteConfigContext so nested child RouteNode and ComponentAgent products remain visible under the parent route context.

Resolve ViewportRequest through none/sole/multiple/open candidate semantics. None with no statically compatible candidate is exact rcNoAvailableVpa/AUR3174 evidence; multiple/open are seams. Never publish a partial transition tree or call a sole static candidate selected/live.

guidance: Start here when effective route-config roots, child configured-context trees, eager-loading recognizer ownership, or RouteConfigContext products change.
Keep RouteConfigContext materialization separate from authored/effective route-config convergence and potential RouteContext/ViewportAgent-candidate topology.

records.rationale: Static rendering/controller products can prove potential router topology before navigation, but live viewport registration and availability remain runtime state. This frontier owns that bridge without manufacturing selected agents or active route trees.
guidance: Start here when work touches au-viewport, ViewportAgent candidates, RouteContext, route child containers, viewport field closure, or static router/rendering topology.
Keep potential topology separate from effective route-config contexts, route instruction parsing, recognition, planned route-tree materialization, and live navigation state.
Use framework.router ViewportAgent/RouteContext relationships and framework.rendering controller rows before changing route rendering semantics.

Preserve template-controller child-view cardinality and none/sole/multiple/open candidate resolution. Only a sole static candidate can cross into a planned transition.

records.summary: RouteInstructionMaterializationProjectPass closes static load/href router resource values into typed navigation and viewport instruction products.
records.rationale: Route instruction materialization depends on rendered router resources, binding source value evaluation, route contexts, and router options. Keep this as an explicit router/template bridge instead of treating load/href as plain attribute strings.
guidance: Start here when load/href custom attributes, object navigation instructions, typed navigation instructions, viewport instruction trees, or open route-expression seams change.

Router resource instructions should materialize only when a concrete owning RouteContext is known through controller/container ancestry or route-config component-definition matching. A reusable component's standalone definition render is not an app-level route instruction site; do not publish a route-context open seam when the same instruction closes under a routed parent render.
Use observation source-value evaluation and template controller/rendering products before changing static router instruction closure.

For dynamic href seams, mirror HrefCustomAttribute exactly: `_resolveIsExternal(...)` gates URL generation, while RouterOptions.useHref=false, non-anchor hosts, or a co-located load attribute only disable click interception and must not be treated as proof of external URL intent.

Anchor `target` values other than `_self` are not automatically disabled in the semantic model: framework `HrefCustomAttribute` disables interception for those targets unless the literal target equals runtime `IWindow.name`. Use `router-href-click-interception-target-open` for that host-contract boundary instead of collapsing `_blank` or named targets into unconditional disabled click handling.

When an open router instruction seam has a binding/value source address, diagnostics-to-action or future edit planning should preserve it as a `runtime-boundary` action target. The target is for intent collection and future planning, not proof that a source edit is already safe.

Use the synthetic `router-dynamic-pattern` pressure fixture before external app pressure when changing href repair behavior; it covers internal string-pattern closure, external-link-like field openness, and bare external-module value boundaries with non-current-window target pressure.

As of the compact app-pressure check on 2026-05-23, the aggregate `router.open-instruction` seam is expected pressure: `router-dynamic-pattern` keeps an external-module href value open while click interception is disabled by `useHref=false` and target comparison remains runtime-open through `router-href-click-interception-target-open`. `router-viewport-resolution-errors` should publish exact AUR3174 `no-available-viewport-agent` diagnostics without adding a parallel repair-intent seam.
Keep route instruction materialization separate from recognizer path matching and route-tree transition compilation.

Closed primitive router-resource values that cannot be route strings, routeable components, or viewport instructions are TypedNavigationInstruction creation issues with instrInvalid / AUR3400 authority. Do not spend this code on classes/functions/promises that are valid framework routeable lanes but currently under-modeled.

Object-form router resource values belong to RouteConfigContext eager path generation before they re-enter the RouteExpression instruction-tree lane. Missing required params for RouteConfig/class components are RouterIssue rows with exact AUR3166 authority; string route ids are framework non-throwing and should not spend that code. Closed instruction children recurse through the generated component RouteConfigContext and preserve child viewport suffixes before lowering back into the static instruction-tree lane.

Inline load multi-bindings with `route` plus object-shaped `params` follow LoadCustomAttribute's component+params branch, not plain RouteExpression parsing. Route-only strings remain RouteExpression input; route+params becomes an eager instruction before static path recognition. Binding-scope param values may use dynamic placeholders when the parameter key is static, but never reuse the route id as the parameter value. Treat `context.bind` as a route-context replacement boundary and keep it open until semantic-runtime models that owning context.

Endpoint selection and parameter substitution are separate phases of eager path generation. RouteInstructionMaterializationProjectPass evaluates each load route value once, selects candidate endpoints before missing params can block path generation, and retains RouteParameterEndpointPlan rows by exact authored HTML-attribute product handle for completion consumers.

Route-parameter completion must consume the retained endpoint plan and Endpoint typed details. Do not reparse a sibling route segment, repeat source-value evaluation, or pool parameter names from app-wide route configs; dynamic or context-open routes keep the completion answer open.

Object-form router resource values may arrive as syntactic object literals or equivalent binding-source values such as state/getter-owned instruction arrays. Keep those reads in RuntimeBindingSourceValueEvaluator and consume the closed object here instead of adding router-local expression shortcuts.

`routerSourceExpressionEvaluationFrame(...)` is the route-instruction bridge from a rendered router-resource site into RuntimeBindingSourceValueEvaluationContext or an explicit open source-value row. It now spends `projectRuntimeBindingSourceValueContextInScope(...)` with the rendered binding table and binding-expression scope projector; if this starts growing, improve source-value projection/context primitives rather than reintroducing router-local expression evaluation or a router-owned source-expression projector.

`route-instruction-source.ts` is the source companion for router resource attributes. Source producers should use it for `load` and `href` so generated simple and inline multi-binding forms stay aligned with LoadCustomAttribute and HrefCustomAttribute instead of becoming app-builder-local string templates.

Equivalent object-form router resource values may also arrive as evaluator-local class instances or tagged-template/function results. Route instruction materialization should consume the closed EvaluationObject/Instance shape and leave New/TaggedTemplate AST semantics with RuntimeBindingSourceValueEvaluator.

Router-resource binding-source reads can consume DI activation facts when the render site has controller/container ancestry. Registered interface state such as resolve(IFoo) belongs to RuntimeBindingSourceActivationContext plus the modeled container, not to route-instruction materialization.

Router-resource binding scope lookup should use the render-context-aware RuntimeInstructionScopeLookup. Custom-attribute controllers are created from a hydration instruction, but the binding expression scope belongs to the controller that rendered the instruction sequence, including synthetic template-controller child views.

String-pattern route expressions may arrive from interpolation, template literals, evaluator-local methods, or direct binary `+` concatenation with binding-scope holes. Consume the shared EvaluationStringPatternValue lane and keep the authored static-prefix rule in the binding-source evaluator, not in router-specific AST shortcuts.

Repeated state-backed href canaries should close through binding-source representative values, evaluator loose nullish equality, and recognizer matching when the static prefix survives. If exact per-item field correlation is needed later, model that as value-flow substrate pressure rather than href-specific lookup logic.

Use `route-expression-parser.ts` when framework semantics branch on RouteExpression node kind. It exposes the expression tree, lowered viewport instructions, and source-backed parser failures for exprUnexpectedSegment / AUR3500 and exprNotDone / AUR3501; do not reparse route strings with ad hoc split logic.

Router issue products remain owned by the router lane even when their source is a template value. API template diagnostics and cursor-info may project `router-framework-error` rows for LSP loci, while AppDiagnostics de-duplicates those projected rows and reads the owning RouterIssues lane. Both projections consume `routerIssueDiagnosticRepairProjection(...)`; only source-role-proven template instruction issues receive `fix-router-instruction` guidance, and the absence of an edit plan remains explicit.

Route-instruction issue provenance should prefer the parser expression source or HTML attribute value address over the broader custom-attribute carrier. A broad carrier span is a fallback evidence address, not a rename/edit locus, once value provenance is available.

records.summary: RouteRecognitionMaterializationProjectPass walks route-recognizer graphs for static viewport instruction paths and publishes RecognizedRoute products.
records.rationale: Recognition is algorithmic router substrate: candidates, endpoint requirements, redirect expansion, parameter extraction, and path collapse all need to remain grounded in route-recognizer semantics before route-tree compilation consumes them.
guidance: Start here when static route recognition, candidate selection, redirect expansion, endpoint requirements, or recognized-route products change.
Cross-check framework.router recognizer mechanics before changing Candidate or EndpointRequirement behavior.
Redirect expansion must use the shared route redirect migration substrate rather than splitting redirect strings on `/`; RouteTree is the diagnostic owner for unsupported RouteExpression node kinds.

A closed static viewport-instruction path with a materialized recognizer, no matching configured route, and no owning route-config fallback is a recognition issue with instrNoFallback / AUR3401 authority.

For nested route expressions such as a parent route with residual child segments, recognition recurses into the routed child's RouteConfigContext after the parent residual match. This keeps child RecognizedRoute, RouteNode, and ComponentAgent products visible instead of relying on a single parent residual row.

A recognized redirect route whose migrated target path cannot be recognized is a redirect-resolution issue with instrUnknownRedirect / AUR3402 authority; semantic-runtime records it during redirect expansion even though the framework throws while creating the RouteTree node.
Keep recognition separate from route-recognizer graph construction and route-tree transition materialization.

Keep row construction in route-projections and answer-envelope mechanics in answer-helpers; this class should stay a public query-method facade.
If router query pressure expands, split along route-config, recognizer, viewport, route-tree, or agent concepts rather than moving methods back into runtime.ts.
Keep route-effect facts sourced from route-query-registry; authoring verification may derive query-only rows from that registry, but should not restate the route product vocabulary by hand.

Route expected-effect helpers can now filter route product rows by fields such as `parameterNames`. If recipes need richer route-tree shape, viewport selection, runtime parameter aggregation, or issue-specific expectations, extend the route expected-effect helper layer before adding ad hoc recipe filters.

records.summary: RouteConfig source contributions converge once into definition and per-use applied products.
records.rationale: Aurelia first creates class-level RouteConfig metadata through RouteConfig._create, then clones or overlays it per child use through _applyChildRouteConfig. Authored occurrence, class definition, and applied use therefore have different identities, execution evidence, and closure rules; one hybrid product forced topology and API consumers to reconstruct framework precedence locally.
guidance: RouteConfigContributionModel owns authored origin, value shape, execution evidence, exact source addresses, field state, and field provenance. It is evidence for convergence, not an effective route config.

RouteConfigModel means a framework-shaped effective product. Definition-stage identity is owned by the target custom-element identity; applied-stage identity is owned by the parent effective config plus the authored child use.

RouteConfigConvergenceProjectPass is the only owner of _create and _applyChildRouteConfig precedence, framework defaults, convention-derived path/id, parent transition/fallback inheritance, repeated-use cloning, and route-config openness. Topology, recognizer, route tree, completion, and API code consume its output without local reconstruction.

Only positively executed Route.configure calls may become winners. Same-module execution order selects the final call; cross-module calls without a proven global order and conditionally unproven calls remain named open evidence rather than using source-file order.

Executed Route.configure contributions read occurrence-local invocation evidence. Unproven source sites may close syntax-owned literals but never replay against final module state. Declarative component references join through ResourceDefinitionIndex: locals use module/local identity, while imports use Program-remapped alias-resolved declaration-module identity.
Instance getRouteConfig declarations preserve the pre-hook effective facts and open every field the runtime hook may override. Do not execute the hook or flatten the whole definition to unknown.

Recursive child application is finite in the static product graph: stop at the repeated authored contribution and publish router-route-config-recursive-application on children instead of silently omitting the recursion or constructing an infinite use tree.

The public Routes query remains one row per source contribution and joins effective fields through contribution-to-config links. Use effectiveUseCount, effectiveVariantCount, and effectiveFieldsStable when one source contribution influences multiple applied products.

Project evaluation must replace a graph-dependency placeholder when the same module is later evaluated as a root, retaining both origin rows. A source-result map entry with evaluation=null is not a completed evaluation and must not hide lazy route resource exports.

records.summary: Static router topology distinguishes potential products from sole-candidate plans and never claims live navigation state.
records.rationale: Aurelia resolves navigation against registered ViewportAgent instances and checks live availability before name and usedBy compatibility. Static template analysis can prove potential topology and sometimes a sole compatible candidate, but cannot prove registration order, availability, guards, scheduling, or activation. Flattening those stages created false selected agents, false AUR3174 issues, and bound viewport values rewritten as defaults.
guidance: Use RouterRealizationStageKind as an orthogonal axis: RouteContext, au-viewport, and ViewportAgent rows are potential; pre-activation RouteTree, RouteNode, and ComponentAgent rows are planned; no current producer may emit live.

Potential viewport presence spends the existing template-controller child-view cardinality. Optional, many, or open presence remains potential and publishes open topology evidence rather than being treated as one live registration.

Viewport name, usedBy, default, and fallback retain independent defaulted, closed, referential, or open state plus exact authored sources. Open bound values must not be rewritten as absent framework defaults.

RuntimeBoundControllerValueTable has two intentional authority modes. Synthetic/cross-resource analysis may use definition/type fallback; a consumer that owns one concrete hydrated controller must use readExactControllerProperty so sibling usage sites cannot lend each other values.

Bound-controller rows carry their source resource's RuntimeBindingExpressionScopeProjector. Evaluate parent-to-child values with the row-owned projector rather than borrowing a consumer's binding-behavior lifecycle across resources.

Viewport matching compares usedBy with the resolved custom-element registration name, while routeable products and public rows preserve authored spelling separately for navigation and explanation. If resolution did not close, keep the resolved name null/open; never borrow the authored class or string label as registration identity.

Candidate resolution is none, sole, multiple, or open. Only sole may seed planned route products. None may publish exact rcNoAvailableVpa/AUR3174 when no statically compatible candidate exists; multiple/open publish a seam and no partial plan.

Do not call a sole static candidate selected or available. Live ViewportAgent._isAvailable, transition guards, scheduling, activation, and current route-tree state remain outside the current semantic-runtime claim.

records.summary: Classify callable framework hooks from the owning Aurelia role, never from global member-name sets.
records.rationale: The former completion path classified every checker member from three global spelling sets. It produced false router and AppTask facts, retained removed names, omitted current names, and disagreed with the framework's role-specific dispatch. The checker, binding-scope, controller, RouteConfig, and framework-declaration products already carried the missing ownership evidence; the repair reconnects those products instead of introducing another hook registry.
guidance: Template completion may read an available ambient BindingScope at member sites as classification evidence without offering binding-scope candidates there or requiring scope evidence from owner types projected through another lane. Dependency admission and candidate projection are separate decisions.

Checker type equality is not component-instance proof: self-typed nested and optional-chained values stay ordinary. Expression-member hook facts require a direct $this, $parent, or boundary this receiver resolved through BindingScope.

Member-owner inspection spends the parser's MemberName continuation class. AwaitingChainSegment retains valid receivers for optional-chain and $parent scope-path frontiers and must not be discarded by frontier-enum matching.

Component lifecycle facts require a callable checker member on a custom-element controller binding context and use the executable runtime-html Controller vocabulary owned by component-lifecycle-source.ts.

Router hook facts additionally require an effective RouteConfig targeting the owner or explicit/inherited framework IRouteViewModel heritage. Route configuration proves duck-typed owners; framework heritage is independent declaration evidence.
Keep getRouteConfig in router configuration and canLoad/loading/loaded/canUnload/unloading in router transition lifecycle. Preserve the product that proves owner role in the inquiry answer.

AppTask phases are registration slots, not view-model hooks. Removed or legacy names such as define, load, unload, detached, and unbound must not enter completion classification without executable framework evidence.
Exact hook signature compatibility is a future diagnostic and presentation question. It must not replace role ownership because the runtime discovers and invokes callable members by role and name.

records.summary: Effective RouterOptions belong to concrete RouterConfiguration DI registration uses per AppRoot; duplicate rooted registration is one causal AUR3168 error with no topology winner.
records.rationale: Configuration source values are definitions and may be unregistered or reused. ContainerRegistrationOperation already records the exact admission use and receiving container, while AppRoot is the runtime ownership boundary consumed by route topology. Spending those existing products removes the project-global first-options-row island and preserves definition/use provenance. The framework's RouteContext.setRoot rejects an ancestor-visible existing IRouteContext, so a definitely executed second registration in one modeled app root is incoherent even though lower-level registration emits additional resource warnings first.
guidance: Derive effective RouterOptions from DI registration spending, never from configuration sequence order or the first recognized customize call.
Retain the configuration-value definition source separately from each registration-use source. One reused value may yield several rooted options products; an unregistered value yields none.

When one modeled AppRoot has several definitely executed RouterConfiguration operations, publish AUR3168 on each operation after the first, relate the first operation, and do not build RouterOptions or route topology for that root.
Keep same-source AUR0153/AUR0154 duplicate router built-in resource rows as raw evidence, but present them as runtime consequences under the causal AUR3168 diagnostic on IDE surfaces.
Use readRouterIssues(...) as the owning enumeration for RouterIssues rows, app summary counts, and cursor diagnostic projection; do not hand-assemble producer lists in each consumer.

App admission still synthesizes root containers and does not spend an explicit new Aurelia(container) argument or authored createChild topology. Common-parent versus forked multi-root analysis belongs in configuration/DI; do not approximate it with router-local source containment or sequence ordering.
